evidence: performance-logging.module.ts: @Module({ providers: [PerformanceLoggingInterceptor, PerformanceLoggingService], exports: [...] }) sets up the service as an injected provider.
performance-logging.interceptor.ts: PerformanceLoggingInterceptor's constructor receives `private readonly performanceLoggingService: PerformanceLoggingService` through DI.
performance-logging.interceptor.ts: the LogPerformance decorator runs `const performanceLoggingService = new PerformanceLoggingService();` on each call, getting around DI.

performance-logging.interceptor.ts: `const startTime = performance.now()` plus `logPerformance({ className, methodName, startTime })` appears in intercept() and again in both the promise and plain-value branches of LogPerformance.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files cover one concern: logging performance timings. performance-logging.module.ts sets up PerformanceLoggingService and PerformanceLoggingInterceptor as injected (DI) providers, and the interceptor receives the service through its constructor. In the same file, the LogPerformance decorator gets around that setup: each call runs `new PerformanceLoggingService()` directly instead of using the module's provider. So any config, dependencies or shared state the service gets through DI are skipped, and the unit uses two different ways to get the service. The timing code (record startTime with performance.now(), get the class and method names, call logPerformance) is also written three times: once in intercept() and twice in LogPerformance (the promise branch and the plain-value branch). Confidence is moderate for two reasons. Decorators often can't use DI, so creating the service directly may be a deliberate trade-off. And the actual logging already lives in the service, which keeps the duplication small.

violations.message: The LogPerformance decorator creates its own PerformanceLoggingService with `new` on each call instead of using the provider that PerformanceLoggingModule sets up through DI. The PerformanceLoggingInterceptor in the same file does use DI, so the module gets the service in two different ways.

The timing code (startTime = performance.now(), getting the class and method names, calling logPerformance) appears in intercept() and twice more in LogPerformance. It should live in one shared helper.
